subject.title: Stuck-session liveness monitor misclassifies healthy processing runs as stale during event-loop stalls

question: Should OpenClaw require live or deterministic proof of a healthy processing run reaching stale_session_state and abort_embedded_run before changing the processing/no-activeWorkKind recovery policy?
rationale: The source path exists, but current tests intentionally depend on stale processing recovery and the report labels the healthy-run abort mechanism as likely rather than confirmed.

options.title: Require proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open until a targeted repro or measurement shows a healthy active run losing activity bookkeeping during an event-loop stall and being aborted.

options.title: Patch classifier now
options.body: Approve a narrow guard for processing/no-activeWorkKind sessions and accept redesigning the existing stale-processing recovery tests around a new policy.

options.title: Fold into liveness cluster
options.body: Handle this with the related stuck-session recovery reports so active_reply_work, queued_work_without_active_run, and event-loop stall behavior are decided together.

recommendation.title: Require proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a targeted repro or measurement shows a healthy active run losing activity bookkeeping during an event-loop stall and being aborted.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus is the most recent recovery-path contributor in the affected diagnostic runtime and is a good routing candidate for the recovery policy call.
